meta.method: deterministic text-line proposal over a georeferenced plate: letter-sized connected components are grouped into single-baseline boxes inside the neatline, and each box centre is projected through the plan 030-D conic transform published in plate-georefs.json. Nothing is read: label_text_ar stays empty until a reviewer fills it.
meta.notOCR: these are proposals, not readings and not tribal claims; the title cartouche, town names and tribal names are all proposed alike because the detector cannot know which is which
knownLimits: a town name printed directly above a tribal name can share one box
a strongly rotated or curved label can split into two proposals
the title cartouche and scale bar are proposed like any other text
meta.confidenceDefinition: 0.45*min(1, letters/10) + 0.35*min(1, meanFill/0.55) + 0.20*heightUniformity; it measures how much the box looks like a printed text line, never how likely it is a tribe
meta.labelCentreNote: a printed label is typeset beside the feature it names, so the box centre can sit up to half the label's width away from that feature (Baghdad's box centre, for instance, reads about 1 degree east of the city). The coordinates locate the proposal, not a surveyed point, and a reviewer's boundary trace must not be inferred from a label centre
meta.certaintyRule: a candidate is `suggested` and must never be rendered as a fact; acceptance is a named reviewer's decision recorded in the history table, and any geometry derived through the transform stays `approximate` (plan 030/032)
